title: IDEA-GP: Instruction-Driven Architecture with Efficient Online Workload Allocation for Geometric Perception
problem: Robotic geometric perception tasks (SLAM, Structure from Motion) involve diverse and dynamically varying computational operators — including point cloud registration, pose graph optimization, bundle adjustment, and feature matching — whose workload fluctuates with environment and task, preventing static mapping to specialized accelerators and causing poor resource utilization.
motivation: Robotic autonomy requires real-time localization and 3D mapping on constrained edge platforms, but the diversity of spatial-positioning operators and runtime variability of geometric workloads make conventional fixed-function accelerators or CPU/GPU solutions either inflexible or too power-hungry.
method: IDEA-GP is an FPGA-based instruction-driven accelerator built around an array of general-purpose computational units (PEs) optimized for spatial-positioning representations such as rotation matrices, quaternions, and homogeneous coordinates. A compiler performs online workload analysis — profiling operator types and sizes at runtime — and emits PE-targeted instructions to dynamically schedule and pipeline optimization sub-problems (e.g., least-squares solve, graph relaxation). This instruction-driven dispatch allows the same PE array to handle the varied compute patterns of SLAM (incremental pose estimation, loop closure) and SfM (bundle adjustment, triangulation) without hardware reconfiguration. The system is deployed on a Xilinx ZCU102 evaluation board.
key_novelty: An instruction-driven online workload allocation compiler that dynamically schedules heterogeneous geometric-perception operators onto a unified PE array at runtime, achieving high resource utilization despite task and environment variability.
contributions: IDEA-GP accelerator architecture: a unified PE array designed for spatial-positioning representations supporting diverse robot pose-related computations.
Online compiler that performs runtime workload analysis and emits instructions to dynamically allocate PE resources across heterogeneous geometric operators.
Demonstrated 7.5x speedup over Intel CPU and 19.7x over ARM CPU on SLAM tasks, and 16.4x over Intel CPU and 41.6x over ARM CPU on SfM tasks on ZCU102.

metrics.speedup: 7.5x over Intel CPU and 19.7x over ARM CPU (SLAM); 16.4x over Intel CPU and 41.6x over ARM CPU (SfM) on Xilinx ZCU102

limitations: Evaluation is on FPGA (ZCU102) rather than an ASIC implementation, so power and area figures do not reflect production-level efficiency; baselines do not include GPU comparisons.
primary_theme: Instruction-driven FPGA accelerator for robotic geometric perception with online workload allocation
